items.name: Serverless Pipe
items.text: Fully managed with no shards to provision; auto-scales and bills by ingested volume. No replay and no multiple consumers.

items.name: Buffering
items.text: Batches records until a size or time hint is met (seconds to minutes). Larger buffers make bigger S3 files; smaller buffers lower latency.

items.name: In-Flight ETL
items.tag: AWS Lambda, AWS Glue Data Catalog
items.text: Runs Lambda transforms, converts JSON to Parquet/ORC via a Glue table schema, and builds Hive-style S3 prefixes with dynamic partitioning.

blocks.heading: Exam Tips & Traps
items: Near real time only (buffering) — sub-second or ms latency means Firehose alone is a trap.
Format conversion needs JSON input + Glue Data Catalog table; convert CSV via Lambda first.
No replay and no multiple consumers — pair Kinesis Data Streams with Firehose for those.
Small buffers make many small S3 files (hurts Athena); Redshift always stages via S3 COPY.

blocks.caption: Pair KDS -> Firehose for real-time alerts/replay plus managed S3 archive.
blocks.heading: Firehose vs Kinesis Data Streams

points: No replay; single managed delivery pipe
